summary: The orders service plus explicit warehouse-partner, deployment, data-residency, load, budget, and recovery constraints for a consequential resilience design.
planted: CONSTRAINTS.md says card capture and the warehouse call currently share one database transaction.
The project runs one container, uses Postgres as its only stateful dependency, must keep order data in the EU, and has half a day per week for engineering.
The partner accepts an order reference as an idempotency key, has a rate limit, and rejects consignments older than fourteen days.
absent_on_purpose: No broker, queue service, event platform, or approved new vendor.
No owner-visible choice between technical implementations.
setup: Copy the base fixture orders-service into an empty scratch directory.
Copy the files in this directory over it.
Run: git init && git add . && git -c user.email=fixture@example.invalid -c user.name=Fixture commit -m 'Fixture base'
end_state_signals: The report compares the repository and Postgres capabilities with maintained alternatives, lifetime cost, failure recovery, migration, and rollback.
Any durable decision cites CONSTRAINTS.md and records rejected alternatives without inventing a product choice.
privacy: Invented storefront and partner, no personal data, credentials, or network use.
